bigo.q: What is the time complexity of accessing arr[i] in an array?
bigo.explain: Arrays use contiguous memory, so the address is computed directly from the index: constant time.

bigo.q: Two nested loops, each running n times, give a time complexity of:
bigo.explain: n iterations of an inner loop that runs n times gives n * n = O(n^2).

arrays.q: Inserting an element at the beginning of an array of n elements costs:
arrays.explain: Every existing element must shift one position to the right.
Contiguous storage is what gives arrays O(1) indexing.

strings.explain: Python strings cannot be modified in place; operations create new strings.

strings.q: Checking whether a string of length n is a palindrome efficiently takes:
strings.explain: Compare characters from both ends with two indices: one pass, O(n).

recursion.explain: The base case stops the recursion.

recursion.q: What happens if a recursive function has no reachable base case?
recursion.explain: Calls keep stacking until the call stack limit is exceeded.

sorting.q: Worst-case time complexity of Bubble Sort:
sorting.explain: Up to n passes of up to n comparisons each.

sorting.q: Which simple sort is stable and fast on nearly sorted input?
sorting.explain: Insertion sort does very little shifting when data is almost sorted (best case O(n)) and keeps equal elements in order.

binsearch.q: Binary search requires the data to be:
binsearch.explain: Discarding half the range only works if order tells you which half to discard.
The search space halves every step.

linkedlist.q: Inserting at the head of a singly linked list takes:
linkedlist.explain: Create a node, point it to the old head, update head: no shifting.

linkedlist.q: Main drawback of a linked list compared with an array:
linkedlist.explain: You must walk from the head to reach the i-th node.

stack.q: Which problem is a classic use of a stack?
options: Shortest path in a weighted graph
stack.explain: Push opening brackets and pop on closing ones.

queue.q: Which algorithm relies on a queue?
queue.explain: BFS processes vertices level by level using a FIFO queue.

hashing.q: Average-case lookup time in a hash table:
hashing.explain: A good hash function maps keys directly to buckets.

hashing.q: Two different keys mapping to the same index is called a:
hashing.explain: Collisions are resolved by chaining or open addressing.

window.q: Sliding window is best suited for:
window.explain: The window grows and shrinks over a contiguous range.

window.q: Finding a pair with a given sum in a sorted array using two pointers takes:
window.explain: Each pointer moves at most n steps in total.

advsort.q: Worst-case time complexity of Merge Sort:
advsort.explain: log n levels of splitting, O(n) merge work per level.

advsort.q: Worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort:
advsort.explain: A bad pivot (e.g. always the smallest) gives unbalanced partitions.

bst.q: An inorder traversal of a BST produces:
bst.explain: Left < Root < Right at every node, so inorder gives sorted output.

bst.q: Search in a completely skewed BST with n nodes costs:
bst.explain: A skewed BST degenerates into a linked list.

heap.q: In a min-heap the smallest element is located at:
heap.explain: The heap property puts the minimum at the root.

heap.q: Building a heap from n elements with bottom-up heapify takes:
heap.explain: Most nodes are near the leaves and sift down very little; the sum is O(n).

trie.q: A trie is best suited for:
trie.explain: Words sharing a prefix share a path from the root.

trie.q: Searching a word of length L in a trie costs:
trie.explain: One step per character, independent of the number of stored words.

graphs.q: Space used by an adjacency list for V vertices and E edges:
graphs.explain: One list per vertex plus one entry per edge.

graphs.q: A connected undirected graph with no cycles is called a:
graphs.explain: A tree is a connected acyclic undirected graph.

traversal.explain: A FIFO queue gives level-by-level exploration.

traversal.q: BFS gives the shortest path (fewest edges) in:
traversal.explain: The first time BFS reaches a vertex is via the fewest edges.

options: Trying choices and undoing them when they fail
backtrack.explain: It explores a decision tree and abandons (prunes) dead ends.

backtrack.q: Which is a classic backtracking problem?
backtrack.explain: Place a queen, recurse, and remove it if the placement leads nowhere.

greedy.q: For activity selection, the correct greedy rule is to pick the activity with the:
greedy.explain: Finishing earliest leaves the most room for later activities.

dp.q: Dynamic programming applies when a problem has:
dp.explain: Reusing stored subproblem answers is the core idea.

dijkstra.q: Dijkstra's algorithm fails when the graph has:
dijkstra.explain: A finalized distance may later need to decrease if a negative edge exists.
It repeatedly extracts the vertex with the smallest tentative distance.

options: Find a set's representative and merge sets
unionfind.explain: find(x) and union(x, y) on disjoint sets.

unionfind.q: Which optimizations make Union-Find nearly O(1) per operation?
options: Path compression and union by rank
unionfind.explain: They keep the trees extremely shallow.

mst.q: How many edges does an MST of a connected graph with V vertices have?
mst.explain: A spanning tree connects V vertices with V - 1 edges.

mst.q: Kruskal's algorithm uses which structure to avoid cycles?
mst.explain: It adds the cheapest edge only if its endpoints are in different sets.

toposort.explain: A cycle makes a valid ordering impossible.

toposort.q: Which algorithm performs topological sort using in-degrees?

advdp.q: Number of states in the 0/1 knapsack DP for n items and capacity W:
advdp.explain: dp[i][w] for each item index and capacity.

advdp.q: Time complexity of the standard LCS DP for strings of lengths m and n:
advdp.explain: One table cell per pair of prefixes, each computed in O(1).
